text:
maya: heads up — getting customer escalations about timeouts + 5xx on hosted inference (eu-west-1) since ~08:15 UTC. SLO probe firing. anyone seeing matching traces?

ashley: saw the probe alert too. dashboard shows 5xx spike starting 08:12, 50m window. probe SLO burn ~4.2%. link: https://grafana.redwood/g/ingress/slo-eu-west1

ben: looking at API gateway logs now. a lot of upstream 502s and 504s with connection_reset / read timeout. sample: `upstream_time=12.3s, backend=runtime-pool-5`

maya: can you paste the fail logs for a request id? CX wants repro steps and timestamps.

ben: here's a recent one: request_id=rt-6f8a9, path=/v1/generate, client=customer-xyz, status=502. stack: `gateway -> runtime-proxy -> grpc timeout`

tom: @ben any resource pressure on runtime nodes? cpu/gpu usage high?

ben: CPU fine, GPUs saturated on a couple nodes. Autoscaler didn't spin up extra capacity — suspect scale-up lag + connection queueing.

ashley: I see increased tail latencies in KV cache hit rate drop too — suggests cache thrash after a rollout? metrics: `kv_cache_hit 0.42 -> 0.12` at 08:10

maya: did we push any runtime or model variants around that time? deploy bot?

sre-bot: DEPLOYMENT_EVENT: runtime-service v1.82 -> v1.83 rolled 08:07-08:09 UTC (canary -> prod).

maya: ok that aligns. maybe v1.83 regen cache or changed attention kernel? could explain KV drop and spike.

tom: quick triage plan: 1) throttle incoming traffic to dedicated lane for critical customers, 2) rollback canary if we confirm correlation, 3) gather traces for gap analysis.

ashley: adding log query (sum of 5xx by backend):
```
index=ingress logs
| where timestamp >= ago(30m)
| where status >= 500
| stats count() by backend, status
| sort by count desc
```

ben: also running a trace gap check — I see lots of requests with missing spans from runtime-proxy to model-runtime between 08:10 and 08:20. possible tracer sampling change in v1.83.

maya: can you get a flamegraph or pprof from an affected runtime node? need to confirm thread/blocking in grpc worker loops.

ben: grabbing pprof now. attaching small excerpt: `pprof: goroutine 129 blocked in recv on stream, net/http2`

tom: that sounds like connection pool exhaustion. what's our max concurrent grpc streams setting?

ashley: default is 250 per connection, but we saw many short-lived connections — runtime-proxy opens many connections per worker. pooling bug could leak streams.

maya: timeline: deploy v1.83 at 08:07, KV cache hit drop at 08:10, 5xx spike 08:12, SLO alert 08:15 — strong correlation. recommend safety rollback to v1.82 asap and keep canary offline until we patch pooling.

ben: initiating rollback to v1.82 now. rolling back canary first. command: `opsctl deploy runtime-service --image v1.82 --to canary`

sre-bot: ROLLBACK_STARTED runtime-service canary -> v1.82 at 08:33 UTC

ashley: after rollback, probe shows 5xx dropping back to baseline within ~4m. KV cache hit trending back up.

tom: good. next steps: 1) postmortem entry, 2) add pooling integ test, 3) increase autoscaler headroom for spikes during rollouts, 4) add detection rule for KV cache drop correlated with deploys.

maya: agree. also need an ops note for support: repro steps for customer: include request ids (rt-6f8a9 and rt-6f8b2), timeframe 08:10-08:40 UTC, and that we rolled back a runtime deployment which resolved the issue.

ben: I'll drop the exact logs into the incident ticket and flag customers impacted.

ashley: putting the trace & log queries used into the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/incident/2041829300

maya: thanks all. filing follow-up RFC for pooling fix and canary autoscale policy. feel free to ping if you see recurrence. :thumbsup:
